Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "this note is about the scanner loan from the northpoint library branch, and the way the dates and equipment are written down should be easy for the next desk worker to follow. on may 12, mira chen borrowed scanner LS-04 for a community oral-history project. she was scanning consent forms at the neighborhood archive room, not taking the scanner for general use. the checkout was recorded at 10:15 a.m., and the return was due on may 15 by 5:00 p.m. those dates matter because the archive room was booked again the following morning, and the forms needed to be back with the project coordinator before then.

at pickup, mira received the scanner, one USB-C cable, a padded sleeve, and two spare batteries. the desk worker, jo, counted the parts with her and wrote them on the loan card. the scanner itself has the asset label LS-04 on the underside, while the loan card is kept in the blue equipment binder. jo connected the scanner to the branch laptop before mira left, and a test scan of one page came through legibly. that was only a pickup check; it did not mean that the full batch had been scanned or that the archive had accepted the files.

mira said the consent forms were in three paper folders, with 46 forms in all. she planned to scan them in the archive room because that room has a large table and a door that can be closed while people are being interviewed nearby. she was not planning to scan the interview audio, and the scanner would not be used to copy identity documents. the forms were already signed, but a few had notes written in the margins. the project coordinator wanted those notes visible in the image, so mira asked jo not to suggest a crop setting that would cut off the page edges.

jo explained that the scanner should stay flat on the table and that the sleeve was for carrying it between the branch and the archive room, not for storage while the unit was running. mira said the archive room had a standard wall outlet and that she would use the supplied cable with the project laptop. the two spare batteries were included in case the outlet was occupied, but no one had decided that battery operation would be needed. if a battery was used, mira was to put it back in the same sleeve pocket after the session so the return count would be simple. the cable was to be wound loosely rather than bent around the power plug.

there was one point about timing that needs to stay plain. if LS-04 has not been returned by 4:30 p.m. on may 15, the desk worker should call the branch coordinator before booking a replacement scanner. that call is not the same as extending the loan, and the note does not say that an extension has been approved. mira said she would phone the desk if the archive session ran late, but she did not ask for a later due time. the coordinator can check the next day's reservations and decide what equipment is available only after hearing the situation.

1. at checkout, record the borrower, asset label, pickup time, due date, and the items counted with the scanner. for this loan, the borrower is mira chen, the asset label is LS-04, the pickup time is 10:15 a.m. on may 12, and the due time is 5:00 p.m. on may 15. list one USB-C cable, one padded sleeve, and two spare batteries, rather than writing only “accessories.” the test scan was one page, and its purpose was to check that the scanner connected to the branch laptop and produced a legible image.

2. on return, count the same items beside the loan card and check the scanner for visible damage. the return check should not assume that the 46 consent forms were all scanned, because the desk does not receive or review the project files. if the borrower reports a problem with the scan, note her words and pass the issue to the coordinator; do not describe a reported problem as a confirmed fault. the blue equipment binder stays at the service desk, and the loan card should be returned to it after the count is recorded.

3. keep the file name for the delivery record exactly as supplied, since the archive coordinator is expecting that name in the handoff list. this is the file name:
delivery-summary.tsv
it refers to the delivery summary, not the scanned consent forms themselves. the loan note can mention that the summary file is expected, but it should not imply that the branch has received it or checked its contents. if mira brings a printed copy, it can be passed to the project coordinator with the other handoff papers; the scanner return and the file handoff are separate items to track.

the archive room booking is for the morning after the scanner is due, and the project coordinator needs the completed forms before that booking begins. that timing explains why the 4:30 call condition is useful, but it does not change the due time or guarantee another scanner. mira said, “I can bring it back before five, unless the room booking runs over.” if she calls because it is running late, the desk worker should record the time of the call and what she says, then contact the branch coordinator as described above. the note should keep the difference clear between the due date, a possible late return, and a request that still needs a decision.", "output": "This note covers the scanner loan from the Northpoint Library branch. The dates and equipment details should be clear enough for the next desk worker to follow. On May 12, Mira Chen borrowed scanner LS-04 for a community oral-history project. She was scanning consent forms at the neighborhood archive room, not using the scanner for general purposes. The checkout was recorded at 10:15 a.m., and the scanner was due back by 5:00 p.m. on May 15. These dates matter because the archive room was booked again the following morning, and the forms needed to be back with the project coordinator before then.

At pickup, Mira received the scanner, one USB-C cable, a padded sleeve, and two spare batteries. Jo, the desk worker, counted the items with her and listed them on the loan card. The scanner’s asset label, LS-04, is on its underside, and the loan card is kept in the blue equipment binder. Before Mira left, Jo connected the scanner to the branch laptop. A test scan of one page came through legibly. This was a pickup check only; it did not mean that the full batch had been scanned or that the archive had accepted the files.

Mira said the consent forms were in three paper folders and that there were 46 forms in total. She planned to scan them in the archive room, which has a large table and a door that can be closed while people are being interviewed nearby. She did not plan to scan the interview audio or copy identity documents with the scanner. The forms were already signed, but a few had notes in the margins. The project coordinator wanted those notes to remain visible in the images, so Mira asked Jo not to suggest a crop setting that would cut off the page edges.

Jo explained that the scanner should remain flat on the table. The padded sleeve was for carrying it between the branch and the archive room, not for storing the scanner while it was running. Mira said the archive room had a standard wall outlet and that she would use the supplied cable with the project laptop. The two spare batteries were included in case the outlet was occupied, but no one had decided that battery power would be needed. If Mira used a battery, she was to put it back in the same sleeve pocket after the session so the return count would be straightforward. The cable should be wound loosely, not bent around the power plug.

The timing condition should be stated clearly. If LS-04 has not been returned by 4:30 p.m. on May 15, the desk worker should call the branch coordinator before booking a replacement scanner. That call is not an extension of the loan, and the note does not say that an extension has been approved. Mira said she would phone the desk if the archive session ran late, but she did not ask for a later due time. The coordinator can check the next day’s reservations and determine what equipment is available only after hearing the situation.

1. At checkout, record the borrower, asset label, pickup time, due date, and items counted with the scanner. For this loan, the borrower is Mira Chen, the asset label is LS-04, the pickup time is 10:15 a.m. on May 12, and the due time is 5:00 p.m. on May 15. List one USB-C cable, one padded sleeve, and two spare batteries rather than writing only “accessories.” The test scan was one page. Its purpose was to check that the scanner connected to the branch laptop and produced a legible image.

2. On return, count the same items beside the loan card and check the scanner for visible damage. Do not assume that all 46 consent forms were scanned, because the desk does not receive or review the project files. If the borrower reports a scanning problem, record her words and pass the issue to the coordinator; do not describe a reported problem as a confirmed fault. The blue equipment binder stays at the service desk, and the loan card should be returned to it after the count is recorded.

3. Keep the delivery-record filename exactly as supplied because the archive coordinator expects that name in the handoff list. The filename is:
delivery-summary.tsv
It refers to the delivery summary, not the scanned consent forms. The loan note can say that the summary file is expected, but it should not imply that the branch has received the file or checked its contents. If Mira brings a printed copy, it can be passed to the project coordinator with the other handoff papers. The scanner return and the file handoff are separate items to track.

The archive room is booked for the morning after the scanner is due, and the project coordinator needs the completed forms before that booking begins. This timing explains why the 4:30 call condition is useful, but it does not change the due time or guarantee another scanner. Mira said, “I can bring it back before five, unless the room booking runs over.” If she calls because the booking is running late, the desk worker should record the call time and what she says, then contact the branch coordinator as described above. The note should distinguish the due date, a possible late return, and a request that still needs a decision."}]
